TextBlock.Text: THEATRE Fiordland approaches
DATE 19 January 2029 · 0520 local
SIDE People's Liberation Army Navy
WINDOW 45 min, closes at 68
Type 039C Yuan-class. Photo: Petty Officer 1st Class Chad J. McNeeley, U.S. Navy · Public domain · cropped
"We are not training for our best day out. We are training for our worst day and then the next day and the day after."
- Wing Commander Tim Hurford, RAAF, 2026

FIORDLAND APPROACHES, 0520. AUSTRAL COMPLIANCE is on the final approach to meet HULL 334. One of Meridian's contractor vessels, FV AUSTRAL WARDEN, has rejected the handover and is closing the tender. It is a Q-ship with a wake-homing torpedo, not another fishing boat. Expect its attack around minute twelve if it is left alone. The Q-ship is declared hostile and may be engaged before it fires.

Your screen still provides the loud decoy on the eastern station, but it needs to be there at minute eight while the tender completes the final leg. The screen is some thirty miles from the rendezvous; HULL 334 is the nearby combat unit and can counter the Q-ship while the screen holds the patrol's attention. Keep enough time for a torpedo to reach the Q-ship before its own shot reaches the slow tender.

Destroy the Q-ship and bring the tender and boat together in the holding box. KIWI 05 remains a protected patrol aircraft. Leave it alone. Keep HULL 334 quiet where possible: classification loses the concealment bonus but does not end the mission. Report the compromise and continue the defence and rendezvous.
The Milford cruise ship and local fishing boats are protected. They are not cover for an indiscriminate attack.
COMMAND NET: A mission-specific tactical report follows eight minutes after the start. It is advice from the command team, not a new sensor detection.
Fleet headquarters, southern tasking
COMMANDER'S INTENT

Complete the rendezvous and protect the tender. The contractor Q-ship is a declared hostile. Kiwi 05 and civil traffic are protected. Concealment earns credit, but losing it does not erase a successful defence.
• Cover the decoy station at minute eight, stop the Q-ship, then bring the tender and Hull 334 to the holding position
• Avoid classification if possible; detection does not end the mission
• Do not attack Kiwi 05 or civil traffic
• Bring the screen off the decoy station intact
• Keep Austral Compliance afloat
• Keep Hull 334 afloat
• Destroy the hostile Q-ship threatening the tender
• Harm no cruise ship or fishing boat
Your screen and its flight; allocated tender Austral Compliance and Type 039C Hull 334. Hostile: one contractor Q-ship. Protected: Kiwi 05, the cruise ship and fishing traffic.

The planned window is 45 minutes. At that minute Command signals that you are behind schedule and holds the line for about 23 minutes more; the operation is closed at 68 minutes and the main task will be recorded as failed.
RULES OF ENGAGEMENT
All designated neutral contacts are protected. A protected neutral loss cancels the operation. Identify before you shoot.
